transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SA), Dr. Laura Chen (Elmcrest CTO), Mark Reyes (Elmcrest Head of Security), Ayesha Patel (Elmcrest AI Lead), Tom Boyd (Elmcrest Infra)

Summary:
Redwood and Elmcrest discussed scoping for a security-focused pilot of Redwood Private/Dedicated to run PHI-related triage and note-summarization workloads. Key topics: SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML + IdP integration, RBAC and audit log requirements, KMS/HSM key management, VPC peering and network egress, pilot success criteria (latency, throughput, quality), and benchmark plan and timeline.

Topics:
- Security/compliance artifacts and controls
- Pilot workload sizing and benchmarks
- Integration plan (SSO, RBAC, VPC)
- Timelines and next steps

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: All right, thanks everyone for joining. I see we have the full team from Elmcrest. Quick intro then we'll jump in -- I know security is top priority here so we'll focus on that and the pilot success criteria.

[00:28] Dr. Laura Chen: Thanks, Sofia. Yes, sorry for the late one for some folks. Our main ask is we want to validate an on-prem / VPC deployment that handles PHI, so the compliance bits are the gating items.

[00:44] Mark Reyes: To add, SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 are must-haves, plus audit logs for all model calls and key access events. We also need SSO via our Okta, SAML-based, and fine-grained RBAC so ops can't accidentally access training data.

[01:12] Jon Park: Understood. Redwood Private supports SOC 2 and ISO controls; we can share our certs. For logs we can stream audit events to your SIEM, and we have KMS integrations for customer-managed keys. Quick question on retention windows — what are you expecting for logs?

[01:35] Mark Reyes: We typically keep audit logs for seven years for legal holds, but for the pilot we need at least 90 days searchable logs. Long-term retention policy will be handled separately.

[02:02] Priya Nair: Noted. For SSO we support SAML SSO and can map groups to RBAC roles in the console. We also support SCIM for provisioning, though that can be staged post-pilot.

[02:25] Ayesha Patel: Re pilot success criteria, we're looking at three buckets: security/compliance validation, performance (latency and throughput), and quality/regression (accuracy on our clinical summaries). For quality we'll provide a labelled set of 500 clinical notes for evaluation.

[02:50] Sofia Martinez: Great — can you share the eval set in anonymized form? Also to set expectations on performance, are you planning burst traffic or steady state?

[03:06] Ayesha Patel: Mostly steady-state for triage: roughly 80 concurrent users during peak with average 1 request per user per minute, plus occasional bursts during batch imports. So estimate about 80–120 QPS during peak and bursts up to ~300 QPS for short periods.

[03:30] Tom Boyd: Network question: we prefer VPC peering into our AWS account; we need details on egress IPs for firewall rules and whether Redwood can support transitive peering.

[03:48] Jon Park: We support VPC peering and private link options. We'll provide a list of egress CIDR ranges and suggested firewall rules. Transitive peering typically isn't needed; we'll work with you on private link.

[04:12] Dr. Laura Chen: One more compliance note: we need evidence of background checks / personnel security for engineers that will have access to the control plane — is that in your SOC 2 scope?

[04:28] Sofia Martinez: Yes, personnel controls and background checks are covered in our SOC 2 report. We'll upload the redacted SOC 2 Type II and our ISO 27001 scope document after the call.

[04:45] Mark Reyes: On KMS, we require customer-managed keys in our KMS with HSM backing. Can you confirm whether Redwood can encrypt model cache and logs with our CMK?

[05:02] Jon Park: Yes, we support CMKs via AWS KMS and can configure encryption at rest for caches and logs. For HSM-backed keys we support integrations with external HSM providers; we can detail that in the security doc.

[05:25] Ayesha Patel: For benchmarking, what's your recommended approach? We want to measure latency p99, p95, average, and throughput for our note-summarization model and also validate cost per 1k tokens.

[05:40] Priya Nair: We'll propose a benchmark plan: (1) dry-run with small synthetic set to validate connectivity and auth, (2) run the Elmcrest eval set against a pinned model variant in Redwood Dedicated (quantized option if you want lower cost), (3) measure latency percentiles, throughput, GPU utilization, and cost per token. We'll provide a spreadsheet template for results.

[06:05] Ayesha Patel: That sounds good. For quality, we need side-by-side compare to our in-house inference to ensure parity or acceptable delta.

[06:20] Sofia Martinez: We often include regression thresholds in the SLOs — e.g., no more than 2% drop in F1 on your clinical summary metric. If beyond that, we can roll back to previous model or run tuned quantization.

[06:38] Mark Reyes: Good, and on logging we need request/response hashes, user id mapping (pseudonymized), and full audit trail for key rotations.

[06:56] Jon Park: We can stream structured audit events that include request ID, model variant, tokens in/out, user mapping (you can choose to pseudonymize before storing), and key rotation events. We also have immutable log storage options.

[07:20] Tom Boyd: For the pilot timeline, what would you propose? We want to start a two-week pilot with a full benchmark in week one and a security validation in week two.

[07:33] Priya Nair: Typical pilot plan: Week 0 (this week) — exchange artifacts and set up access. Week 1 — connectivity and small-scale benchmark run. Week 2 — full workload benchmark and compliance validation with your security team. Pilot wrap and decision at end of week 2. That lines up with your two-week ask.

[07:52] Dr. Laura Chen: Sounds reasonable. I want to call out data residency — specific PHI cannot leave our region, so if you host any components, they must be in our AWS us-east-2 region or in our VPC.

[08:09] Sofia Martinez: Understood — for Redwood Private we'll deploy into your VPC in us-east-2; no PHI will traverse public internet. We'll note that in the SOW.

[08:24] Ayesha Patel: On RBAC, we need role separation: clinical reviewers, data engineers, and security admins with least privilege. Can we map that during pilot?

[08:39] Jon Park: Yes, we can create custom roles and map SAML groups to those roles. We'll document recommended least-privilege roles for the pilot and demo the mapping during setup.

[08:56] Mark Reyes: For the legal side, we need encryption-in-transit details and whether you support TLS 1.3-only endpoints and mutual TLS for certain service-to-service calls.

[09:10] Priya Nair: We support TLS 1.3 and can enable mTLS for service endpoints where required. We'll detail cipher suites and endpoint URLs in the security appendix.

[09:28] Sofia Martinez: Moving to success criteria numbers — let's be explicit so both sides can sign-off. Mark, Laura, Ayesha, what would be a pass for security?

[09:40] Mark Reyes: Pass for security: received SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 artifacts, successful SAML SSO authentication, RBAC roles configured as requested, audit events streaming to our SIEM and searchable for 90 days, CMK encryption verified.

[09:58] Ayesha Patel: For performance: p95 latency under 400ms for our typical summarization request size (~1k tokens in, 150 tokens out) and ability to sustain 120 QPS steady with acceptable p99 under 1.2s. Cost per 1k tokens should be within 20% of your estimate in the pricing deck.

[10:22] Dr. Laura Chen: For quality: F1 drop less than 2% vs our baseline; if not, we consider tuning or different model variant.

[10:34] Jon Park: I'll capture those as measurable pass/fail criteria in the benchmark spreadsheet.

[10:42] Ayesha Patel: One operational question: will Redwood provision a test service account for us with limited credits or will we run on our committed account?

[10:52] Sofia Martinez: For the pilot we'll provide a dedicated sandbox instance under Redwood Dedicated in your VPC. Billing will be handled under a short-term pilot invoice or a trial credit arrangement — we can confirm after this call.

[11:10] Tom Boyd: About firewall rules — we need the list of IPs and a step-by-step for establishing VPC peering or private link. Can you provide an ops runbook?

[11:24] Jon Park: Yes, we'll share an ops runbook with the exact CIDRs, ports (443 for management plane, and defined ports for telemetry), and step-by-step for AWS PrivateLink. We'll also include a checklist for security validation.

[11:40] Mark Reyes: Ok. Also want to ensure your engineers who run the benchmark have signed NDAs and are covered under our DPA.

[11:50] Sofia Martinez: Redwood will sign the DPA and NDA for the pilot; we'll attach that to the SOW.

[12:02] Ayesha Patel: Can you also capture any potential fallbacks? If performance is off, do you auto-fallback to a different model or route to hosted instance? We need clarity on reliability behavior during pilot.

[12:18] Priya Nair: For pilot we recommend a single pinned variant to keep results consistent. If we see performance issues we can swap to a different quantization profile or a larger instance. We can also configure automatic fallbacks but we'll document that as part of the pilot runbook.

[12:40] Dr. Laura Chen: Timeline check — you mentioned providing SOC artifacts by Monday. Will we have a dedicated SE for setup during the week of 6/17?

[12:52] Sofia Martinez: Yes, Jon will be the SE leading setup and Priya will support architecture. We'll schedule 3 one-hour sessions: connectivity, auth/RBAC mapping, and benchmark run.

[13:10] Jon Park: I'll propose times in the follow-up calendar invite. Also I'll include the benchmark spreadsheet and the SAML metadata exchange checklist.

[13:25] Mark Reyes: For the benchmark we'll need GPU utilization metrics and model warmup strategy documented so we can reproduce.

[13:38] Priya Nair: We'll include GPU metrics (util, memory, temp), KV cache hit rates, batch sizes, and warmup tips. We'll also note quantization differences and how they impact quality and throughput.

[13:55] Ayesha Patel: Ok that's helpful. Any concerns about data leakage from cache / reuse of KV cache between tenants? We must ensure strict isolation.

[14:08] Jon Park: Under Dedicated/VPC deployment each tenant's KV cache is isolated. We have strict multi-tenant separation and can demonstrate that in the runbook.

[14:22] Dr. Laura Chen: One more item: audit log retention and export. For legal holds we may need an export capability to archive logs offsite.

[14:33] Sofia Martinez: We support exporting logs to S3 or streaming to your SIEM; we'll include retention and export steps in the runbook.

[14:46] Mark Reyes: Great. Anything else on compliance?

[14:51] Tom Boyd: N/A from infra.

[14:54] Ayesha Patel: I have one last thing — can you confirm how model updates are handled during pilot? We need deterministic model versions.

[15:03] Jon Park: We'll pin a model version for the duration of the pilot and only update with explicit change-control. We'll also capture model hashes and config in the audit log.

[15:18] Sofia Martinez: Okay let's recap next steps: Redwood will upload SOC2/ISO artifacts, share ops runbook, provide benchmark spreadsheet and SAML metadata flow; Elmcrest will share anonymized eval set, success criteria spreadsheet, and confirm VPC peering windows. We'll set the pilot kickoff for 2028-06-20 if all artifacts are in place.

[15:40] Dr. Laura Chen: That works. Please mark the SSO test window as 6/17-6/18.

[15:47] Jon Park: noted. I'll send invites and the runbook links.

[15:54] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.

[16:00] (crosstalk / small talk)

End of transcript.
